macro_markets.query: What are the most important macroeconomic and stock market news and developments from the past 24 hours? Include major index movements, Fed/central bank news, and significant company earnings or announcements.

items.title: Fed holds interest rates steady
items.summary: The Federal Reserve kept its benchmark rate at 3.75%–4.00% in a 10–2 vote, while officials said inflation remains elevated and gave no clear signal on a December move. Two policymakers dissented in favor of a 25-basis-point hike.

items.title: Major U.S. indexes close modestly higher
items.summary: The Dow rose 0.19% to 52,475.10, the S&P 500 gained 0.28% to 7,743.98, and the Nasdaq advanced 0.27% to 26,549.85 after the Fed decision.

items.title: Alphabet earnings pressure technology futures
items.summary: Alphabet reported a 25% increase in third-quarter revenue to $127.6 billion, but its advertising revenue reportedly fell short of expectations, weighing on shares and sending Nasdaq-100 futures lower in overnight trading.

items.title: Microsoft reports strong cloud growth
items.summary: Microsoft posted quarterly revenue of $92.28 billion, up 19% year over year, with Azure cloud growth accelerating 48%. Its shares rose in extended trading after the results.

items.title: Oracle shares surge on long-term outlook
items.summary: Oracle shares jumped about 11% after the company issued an ambitious long-term cash-flow and revenue outlook, helping support investor confidence in artificial-intelligence infrastructure spending.

items.title: Asian markets mixed as semiconductor stocks rally
items.summary: Asian trading was volatile, with Japan’s Nikkei 225 ending about 1% higher as Advantest rose after lifting its earnings forecast. South Korean and Taiwanese technology shares also advanced, while some regional markets declined.

crypto_news.query: What are the most significant cryptocurrency and blockchain news from the past 24 hours? Include major price movements, regulatory news, and notable project developments.

items.title: Bitcoin slips below $81,000 as major tokens decline
items.summary: Bitcoin fell about 0.83% over 24 hours and traded below $81,000. Ether declined 1.75% to about $2,312, while Cardano posted the largest loss among several major tokens at roughly 4.06%.[2][3][5]

items.title: OCC publishes federal stablecoin rule
items.summary: The U.S. Office of the Comptroller of the Currency published rules for permitted payment stablecoin issuers and foreign payment stablecoin issuers under its jurisdiction. The rule is scheduled to take effect January 18, 2027.[2][5]

items.title: Swiss regulator approves first retail fund holding bitcoin directly
items.summary: FINMA approved Switzerland’s first retail exchange-traded fund that invests directly in bitcoin, classifying it as an alternative investment fund with specific risk provisions.[4]

items.title: Bitcoin ETFs record $137 million in daily inflows
items.summary: U.S. spot bitcoin exchange-traded funds reportedly attracted $137 million in daily inflows, pushing October’s aggregate flows back into positive territory at $111 million.[7][10]

items.title: Cysic suspends bridge after unauthorized CYS minting
items.summary: Cysic suspended its cross-chain bridge after an unauthorized mint of 10 million CYS tokens on BNB Smart Chain, making the incident one of the day’s notable blockchain security developments.[4]

items.title: Mirae Asset issues tokenized note on Solana
items.summary: Mirae Asset Securities Hong Kong completed issuance of a U.S.-dollar-denominated, six-month floating-rate financing note on Solana for qualified institutional investors.[1]

items.title: Google previews split-key crypto custody service for banks
items.summary: Google Cloud previewed a multi-party computation service that allows financial institutions to jointly authorize and sign crypto transactions without any single party holding the complete private key. Commercial availability is planned for early 2027.[4][10]

items.title: Large holder sells more than $100 million in Solana
items.summary: An unidentified whale reportedly sold about 1.02 million SOL, valued at approximately $104 million, over five days.[5]

ai_news.query: What are the most important artificial intelligence and machine learning news and developments from the past 24 hours? Include new model releases, company announcements, research breakthroughs, and industry trends.

items.title: Google unveils Gemini 4 Carbon AI model
items.summary: Google introduced Gemini 4 Carbon, a frontier model focused on cybersecurity, coding, and long-horizon tasks. Initial access is reportedly restricted to selected cybersecurity partners.

items.title: OpenAI releases GPT-6.1 Terra
items.summary: OpenAI launched GPT-6.1 Terra, targeting visual reasoning and computer-use applications, with pricing reportedly below comparable previous models.

items.title: Google DeepMind announces Genie 4 world model
items.summary: Google DeepMind introduced Genie 4, a research-preview world model that generates interactive 3D environments with visuals, sound, dialogue, and natural-language scene changes.

items.title: NVIDIA releases Nemotron 3.5 Transcribe
items.summary: NVIDIA released an open-weight speech model supporting transcription, speaker attribution, translation, and audio question answering across 40 languages. Its associated Granary v2 data pipeline was also made public.

items.title: Anthropic adds enterprise AI spending transparency tools
items.summary: Anthropic introduced reporting tools intended to help enterprise customers track AI usage costs, productivity, and return on investment as adoption of Claude Code increases.

items.title: Microsoft reports record revenue driven by cloud and AI
items.summary: Microsoft reported $92.3 billion in quarterly revenue, with cloud and AI demand cited as major contributors. The company also reported $10 billion in revenue from OpenAI-related commercial deals.

items.title: Guidewire agrees to acquire Hyperexponential
items.summary: Guidewire announced a $1.7 billion cash acquisition of AI underwriting startup Hyperexponential, aiming to add AI-agent capabilities for insurance underwriting and pricing.

items.title: FuriosaAI raises $620 million
items.summary: South Korean AI-chip startup FuriosaAI raised $620 million in Series D funding, reportedly bringing its valuation to $2.9 billion.

items.title: MemTensor open-sources memory-native foundation models
items.summary: Shanghai-based MemTensor open-sourced MemT 1.0, a pair of foundation models designed to incorporate persistent, updateable memory alongside Transformer attention.

items.title: OpenAI and Anthropic models reportedly challenge computational-complexity assumptions
items.summary: Reports describe results from frontier models that may bear on the Exponential Time Hypothesis, with potential implications for theoretical computer science and cryptography. The claims require independent technical validation.
